statusWithCorrectParams: 200 (correct raw UUID personId returns the resolved policy: {"standardHoursPerWeek":40,"maxOvertimeHoursPerWeek":8,"source":"organization",...})
rootCause: The controller (src/modules/overtime/presentation/overtime.controller.ts:57) binds the path param with `@Param('personId')` and NO `ParseUUIDPipe`, then passes the raw string straight into OvertimeResolverService.resolve (src/modules/overtime/application/overtime-resolver.service.ts:34-42) which runs `prisma.overtimeException.findFirst({ where: { personId } })`. The personId column is a UUID, so Prisma throws PrismaClientKnownRequestError 'Inconsistent column data: Error creating UUID' for any non-UUID input. That error is unguarded, so the global filter maps it to HTTP 500 instead of a 400. This endpoint takes NO query params, so 'no query params' is irrelevant; the trigger is purely a non-UUID path param. Peer endpoints (/api/people/:id/profile, /skills, /360, /suggested-positions) all use ParseUUIDPipe and correctly return 400 for a usr_ publicId — this route is the outlier that omits the pipe.

    at $n.handleRequestError (/app/node_modules/@prisma/client/runtime/library.js:121:7315)
    at $n.request (/app/node_modules/@prisma/client/runtime/library.js:121:6307)

    at async OvertimeController.resolve (/app/dist/src/modules/overtime/presentation/overtime.controller.js:46:24)
suggestedFix: Add ParseUUIDPipe to the path param to convert bad input into a 400: `@Param('personId', ParseUUIDPipe) personId: string`. ParseUUIDPipe is already imported in this controller (used on removePolicy). This matches the convention of every other personId path-param route in the codebase. (Severity is P2 because the endpoint is currently dead code — fetchResolvedPolicy in frontend/src/lib/api/overtime.ts:113 has ZERO callers in the UI — so no real user flow hits the 500 today; with correct UUID input it returns 200.)
uiCaller: frontend/src/lib/api/overtime.ts:113 fetchResolvedPolicy(personId) -> httpGet(`/overtime/resolve/${personId}`). This function has NO callers anywhere in frontend/src (verified by grep). If it were wired to a personId from auth principal it would send a raw UUID (200). The browser convention (no UUIDs in URLs; use publicId usr_...) means a future caller would plausibly send a usr_ publicId and hit the 500 — which is why the missing ParseUUIDPipe is still a latent defect.
